title: Graph networks to understand glass dynamics
summary: The networks predict particle mobility in simulated glasses; perturbing the network reveals growing spatial correlations as the glass transition is approached. Evidence comes from simulations: the learned correlation length does not translate directly into a measurable physical quantity.

evidence.tested: Networks trained on simulated glasses predicted particle mobility and were checked against simulation ground truth, outperforming physics-inspired and state-of-the-art baselines (96% correlation at short timescales, 64% at relaxation time).
evidence.unknown: The network's correlation length cannot be directly converted into a measurable physical quantity; it remains an open debate; the work models simulated glasses, not physical samples.
evidence.ai_role: Graph neural networks predicted particle mobility and probed spatial correlations by perturbing particles in shells around a marked particle.
